title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent hawkish signals from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, including at Jackson Hole, have elevated expectations for a 25-basis-point rate increase at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, aligning with trader consensus pricing around 57-68% odds for that outcome. Persistent PCE inflation near 3.4-3.7%, well above the 2% target and driven partly by energy supply pressures from Middle East developments, has reinforced the case for tightening despite a stable but softening labor market, where July payrolls declined modestly and unemployment held near 4.1%. The July hold drew dissents favoring action, and markets interpret the Fed's communication as prioritizing credibility on price stability. A no-change decision remains viable at roughly 40% odds if incoming August data shows further cooling, though probabilities for larger moves or cuts stay minimal given current indicators.

The left-handed Frenchman, whose spin-heavy game relies heavily on that wrist, had already suffered first-round exits at Roland-Garros and Wimbledon. Sweeny, a 25-year-old Australian wildcard ranked around No. 123 with a career-high near 121, brought momentum from his Australian Open win over Gael Monfils and strong Challenger results. Their first meeting on outdoor hard courts saw Sweeny lead 7-6(4), 6-4, 3-0 before Moutet retired, highlighting how injury concerns shifted implied probabilities toward the underdog despite Moutet’s higher ranking.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination market reflects a fragmented field with no declared candidates and traders assigning roughly comparable implied probabilities to several contenders amid shifting early polls. Recent surveys, including a late August Morning Consult poll, show Kamala Harris retaining a national lead while Jon Ossoff posts consistent gains and Gavin Newsom slips, mirroring prediction-market movement that has elevated Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Ossoff ahead of Newsom. Key dynamics include AOC’s sustained visibility among progressives and refusal to rule out a bid, Ossoff’s rising profile through Senate reelection positioning in Georgia, and the DNC’s finalized primary calendar front-loading diverse states such as South Carolina. With attention fixed on November 2026 midterms before formal entries, the tight pricing underscores uncertainty over which profiles—progressive, battleground-state, or gubernatorial—will consolidate support once campaigning intensifies.

On the Democratic side, a fragmented field keeps Jon Ossoff at 11.5%, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 10.8%, and Gavin Newsom at 8.6% competitive, with no candidate exceeding 30% in national primary surveys. Key differentiators include battleground-state records, progressive versus moderate appeal, and fundraising capacity ahead of post-2026 midterm announcements. Support could consolidate behind frontrunners via endorsements, debate performances, or shifts in swing-state polling that narrow the wide field.
